ai.headline: RAG Architecture Tradeoffs: Standard vs Graph RAG vs Agentic RAG
ai.body: ByteByteGo's breakdown codifies production selection criteria: Standard RAG for speed-sensitive doc retrieval, Graph RAG for structured knowledge domains (legal, compliance, biomedical) where entity relationships matter, and Agentic RAG for multi-step reasoning with self-correction loops. Key failure mode: Standard RAG has no catch mechanism for wrong chunk retrieval; Agentic RAG adds a verification agent that re-retrieves on failure. Graph RAG's global search path skips vector/graph entirely, batching community reports for LLM relevance scoring — an underappreciated pattern for broad thematic queries.

sec.headline: API Security Checklist: BOLA Still Top Vulnerability, PKCE/mTLS Baseline
sec.body: ByteByteGo's API security summary flags BOLA (Broken Object Level Authorization) as the persistent top API vulnerability, requiring object-, function-, and field-level permission checks per request — not just route-level auth. Key reminders relevant to IAM work: implicit and password grants should be fully deprecated, short-lived tokens with PKCE for public clients, mTLS between internal services, and HSM-backed vault rotation for signing keys. Shadow API inventory is called out explicitly — you can't secure endpoints you don't know exist.

swe.headline: Redis 8 Ships Vector Set as Native Data Structure, Completing RAG Infrastructure Stack
swe.body: Redis 8 adds Vector Set as a built-in data type alongside the existing ten structures, enabling approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings natively — previously requiring RedisSearch or external tooling. This consolidates the RAG retrieval layer into Redis alongside Streams (append-only log with consumer groups and per-consumer offset tracking) and Time Series (with retention and downsampling). Architecturally significant for teams using Redis as a unified data plane across caching, queuing, and now AI retrieval.

mkt.headline: Oracle Posts Worst Week Since 2001 Dot-Com Bust on AI Investment Concerns
mkt.body: Oracle fell 19% on the week as investors questioned the returns on its AI infrastructure buildout, marking its worst weekly performance since the 2001 dot-com collapse. This follows a broader pattern of AI skepticism dragging chip and cloud-adjacent names, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both closing the week down. Relevant signal for MSFT, AMZN, and GOOGL positioning: market is beginning to price in execution risk on AI capex, not just opportunity.

mkt.headline: California Billionaire Tax Act on November Ballot: 5% One-Time Levy on $1.1B+ Residents
mkt.body: A union-backed initiative imposing a one-time 5% tax on California billionaires (residents since Jan 1) qualified for the November ballot, projected to raise $100B over five years. Sergey Brin — who relocated to Nevada — has contributed the majority of $100M+ in counter-campaign funding via Building a Better California. At 54% voter support in May polling, passage is plausible; if enacted, could accelerate high-net-worth tech founder/executive relocations already underway.
